result.document_summary: San Francisco Rent Board info page summarizing the 17 just cause reasons for eviction under the SF Rent Ordinance (Admin. Code ch. 37, § 37.9(a)) and which tenancies are covered.
result.notes: The page gives no effective date for the just cause requirement, so effective_date is empty. Coverage is described only generally (units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limits); the page does not state the base coverage tests, so coverage is left empty. Relocation assistance and notice requirements are not described on this page.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, which must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from the rent increase limits (such as units first receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, and some tenancies regulated by another agency).
rules.exemptions_text: The page does not list exemptions from the eviction provisions; it states that some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits remain subject to just cause eviction rules.
rules.interaction: Tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits (post-June 13, 1979 construction, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated rents) are still subject to the just cause eviction provisions. Ellis Act withdrawals are recognized as one just cause reason.
